purpose: cjson is a lightweight C library for parsing and generating JSON.

functions.cJSON_AddArrayToObject: `cJSON_AddArrayToObject` creates a new empty JSON array and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it when you want to create an array member directly. On success it returns the array item; on failure it deletes the array and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringReference: Creates a JSON string node that **references** an existing C string. Use it when the string is managed elsewhere; `cJSON_Delete` won’t free `valuestring`. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject: Replaces the object member named `string` with `newitem`. Use it on a cJSON object; it returns `cJSON_bool` success/failure. It does not duplicate `newitem`, so pass ownership carefully. If the key isn’t found or `object` is invalid, it fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateBool: Creates a new cJSON boolean item. Pass `cJSON_bool` value; nonzero becomes `cJSON_True`, zero becomes `cJSON_False`. Returns a newly allocated `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_AddNullToObject: Creates a JSON `null` item and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to build objects conveniently. Returns the added item on success; returns `NULL` if creation/addition fails, and then the temporary item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_Print: `cJSON_Print` renders a `cJSON` value into a newly allocated, pretty-printed JSON text string using the global hooks. Use it on a valid `cJSON*`; the caller owns the returned `char*` and must free it. Returns `NULL` on failure.
functions.cJSON_IsNull: `cJSON_IsNull` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON `null` value. Use it on a `cJSON*` to test type safely. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `item->type & 0xFF == cJSON_NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetStringValue: `cJSON_GetStringValue` returns `item->valuestring` only if `item` is a JSON string; otherwise it returns `NULL`. Use it to safely read a string value after checking/expecting a string item. It does not convert types or allocate memory.
functions.cJSON_Parse: `cJSON_Parse` is a simple wrapper for `cJSON_ParseWithOpts(value, 0, 0)`. Use it to parse a JSON string into a `cJSON*`. On success, free the result with `cJSON_Delete`; on invalid JSON, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddNumberToObject: Adds a numeric child to a JSON object. Use with a valid `cJSON` object and key name; it creates a number item and inserts it. On success returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddStringToObject: Creates a JSON string member in an object. Use it as `cJSON_AddStringToObject(obj, "key", "value")`. It builds a string item, adds it to `object`, returns the new item on success, or `NULL` if add fails; on failure it deletes the created item.
functions.cJSON_CreateTrue: `cJSON_CreateTrue()` allocates a new `cJSON` item and sets its type to `cJSON_True`. Use it to create a JSON boolean `true` value. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; otherwise the caller owns the returned item.
functions.cJSON_CreateString:
Creates a new `cJSON` string item from a C string. Use it to build JSON values; it allocates a new node and duplicates `string`. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure, and if duplication fails the item is deleted.
Yes, this is API misuse. cJSON_CreateString expects a valid NUL-terminated C string. Do not pass raw fuzzer bytes or arbitrary binary buffers directly (for example, casting Data to const char *). Ensure the input is copied into a buffer of size Size+1 and explicitly terminated with '\0' before calling, or only pass strings created by a helper like make_cstring(). If the data may contain embedded NULs or is not textual, avoid cJSON_CreateString for that buffer unless you first sanitize/encode it into a proper C string.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromArray: Detaches and returns the item at index `which` from a cJSON array without deleting it. Use a non-negative index; negative returns `NULL`. If the index is out of range or array/item is invalid, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateObject: `cJSON_CreateObject()` allocates a new empty `cJSON` item and marks it as `cJSON_Object`. Use it as the root or a child object, then add members with cJSON add APIs. Returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateFalse: Creates a new `cJSON` boolean item set to false. Use it when building a JSON tree programmatically. It allocates a new node with `cJSON_New_Item`; on success `type` is `cJSON_False`, otherwise it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_free: `cJSON_free` releases memory allocated by cJSON using the active deallocator (`global_hooks.deallocate`). Use it to free cJSON-owned allocations. Passing `NULL` is typically safe if the deallocator allows it. Setting the local pointer to `NULL` has no effect on the caller.
functions.cJSON_CreateNull: `cJSON_CreateNull()` allocates a new `cJSON` item and marks it as `cJSON_NULL`. Use it when you need a JSON `null` value in a tree. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; otherwise the returned item is ready to add to a parent.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToArray: `cJSON_AddItemToArray` appends an existing `cJSON` item to a JSON array. Use it after creating/parsing the item. It returns `true` on success, `false` if the array/item is invalid or insertion fails.
functions.cJSON_PrintBuffered: `cJSON_PrintBuffered` renders a cJSON tree to text using a preallocated buffer to reduce reallocations. Use a nonnegative `prebuffer` guess; `fmt=0` unformatted, `fmt=1` pretty-printed. Returns `NULL` on negative size, alloc failure, or print failure.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItem: `cJSON_GetObjectItem` fetches a child item from a JSON object by key, using case-insensitive matching. Pass an object node and the key string. It returns the matching `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if `object`/`string` is invalid or no match is found.
functions.cJSON_HasObjectItem: `cJSON_HasObjectItem` checks whether an object contains a member with the given key. Use it with a `cJSON` object and a key string. It returns `1` if `cJSON_GetObjectItem` finds it, otherwise `0` (including when absent or lookup fails).
functions.cJSON_GetArrayItem: `cJSON_GetArrayItem` retrieves the array element at a 0-based index. Pass a `cJSON` array and a non-negative `index`; negative indices return `NULL`. If the index is out of range or `array` isn’t valid, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObject: Adds `item` to a JSON object under key `string`. Use it with an object node and a valid `cJSON*` item; it returns `cJSON_bool`. It delegates to internal `add_item_to_object(...)` with global hooks and `false` for the last flag.
functions.cJSON_IsTrue: `cJSON_IsTrue` is a small type-check helper: it tells whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean `true`. Use it on a `cJSON*` node. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-`true` item; otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_AddTrueToObject: Adds a JSON boolean `true` member to an object. Use with a valid `cJSON` object and key name; it creates a true item, inserts it, and returns it on success. If insertion fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsArray: `cJSON_IsArray` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a JSON array. Use it to test an item before array-specific handling. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when the item’s base type is `cJSON_Array`.
functions.cJSON_AddFalseToObject: `cJSON_AddFalseToObject` creates a `false` JSON item and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it for object members only. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject: Adds `item` to `object` under `string` as a **reference** (not a deep copy). Use it when you want shared JSON nodes. Returns `false` if `object` or `string` is `NULL`; otherwise it delegates to `add_item_to_object` with `create_reference(item, ...)`.
functions.cJSON_IsInvalid: `cJSON_IsInvalid` checks whether a `cJSON*` item is non-NULL and has base type `cJSON_Invalid`. Use it to test an item’s type before handling it. Returns `false` for `NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `item->type & 0xFF == cJSON_Invalid`.
functions.cJSON_IsObject: `cJSON_IsObject` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a non-NULL JSON object. Use it before treating an item as an object. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-object type, and `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Object`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Detaches and returns the object member whose key matches `string` case-sensitively. Use it on a JSON object to remove an item without deleting it. If `object`/key is missing or no match is found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS: Adds `item` to `object` using a const key string. Use for string literals or other guaranteed-long-lived strings. It marks the key as const, so cJSON won’t free it; don’t write to `item->string` unless `cJSON_StringIsConst` is clear.
functions.cJSON_AddRawToObject: Adds a raw JSON value to an object under `name`. Use it when `raw` is already valid JSON text and should be inserted unparsed. Returns the new item on success, `NULL` on failure; on failure it deletes the created item.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer: Replaces `item` in `parent` with `replacement` using pointers, preserving list order and shifting later items right. Use only when `item` is already a child of `parent`. Returns `true` on success; `false` if args are NULL. If `replacement==item`, it’s a no-op and returns `true`.
functions.cJSON_IsBool: `cJSON_IsBool` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a boolean (`true` or `false`). Use it to test an item before reading it as a bool. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for non-bool types; otherwise `true` if `type` has `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_CreateNumber: `cJSON_CreateNumber` creates a new `cJSON` number item from a `double`. Use it to build JSON numeric values. On success it sets type to `cJSON_Number`, stores `valuedouble`, and saturates `valueint` to `INT_MAX/INT_MIN` on overflow; returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_IsFalse: `cJSON_IsFalse` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a non-NULL item whose base type is `cJSON_False`. Use it to test JSON booleans before reading values. Returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-false type.
functions.cJSON_SetValuestring: `cJSON_SetValuestring` updates the `valuestring` of an existing `cJSON_String` only. Use it on non-NULL, non-reference string items with a valid current `valuestring`. It returns the new stored string on success, `NULL` if type/args are invalid, corrupted, or the source overlaps unsafely.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringArray: Creates a cJSON array from `count` C strings. Use with a non-NULL `strings` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL on invalid input, array creation failure, or any string item allocation failure; on failure it deletes the partial array.
functions.cJSON_CreateFloatArray: Creates a JSON array from a `float` list. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure; on success, each float is converted to a JSON number, and the array is deleted if any element creation fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateDoubleArray: Creates a JSON array from a `double` list. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns `NULL` on invalid input or allocation failure; on partial failure it deletes the array and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_malloc: `cJSON_malloc` is a thin wrapper around the allocator set by `cJSON_InitHooks`. Use it when you need cJSON’s configured allocation behavior. It simply calls `global_hooks.allocate(size)` and returns that pointer; behavior depends entirely on the installed hook.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive: Returns the child item in a JSON object whose key exactly matches `string` (case-sensitive). Use it on a `cJSON` object node; if `object` is NULL, not an object, or no key matches, it returns NULL.
functions.cJSON_IsRaw: `cJSON_IsRaw` checks whether a `cJSON` item is of type `cJSON_Raw`. Use it to test an item before treating it as raw JSON text. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Raw`.
functions.cJSON_CreateRaw: Creates a `cJSON_Raw` item holding a copied raw JSON text string. Use it when you want cJSON to store preformatted JSON without parsing it. If allocation or string duplication fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddObjectToObject: Creates a new empty JSON object and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it on an existing cJSON object. Returns the new child object on success, or `NULL` if creation/addition fails; on failure, the temp object is deleted.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive: Replaces an object member by key using case-sensitive match. Use with a cJSON object, key string, and new item. Returns true on success; false if object/key not found or inputs are invalid. It updates the existing entry in place.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLength: `cJSON_ParseWithLength` is a convenience wrapper for parsing JSON from a non-NUL-terminated buffer. Use it when you know the exact byte length. It simply calls `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(value, buffer_length, 0, 0)`, so behavior matches that parser with default options.
functions.cJSON_PrintPreallocated: `cJSON_PrintPreallocated` renders a cJSON item into an already-allocated buffer. Use it with a non-NULL buffer and nonnegative length; it sets noalloc mode and returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. If the buffer is too small, printing fails.
functions.cJSON_GetErrorPtr: `cJSON_GetErrorPtr()` returns a pointer into the input JSON at the last parse error. Use it after `cJSON_Parse()` fails to locate the error; it returns `NULL`/0 when parsing succeeds. You may need to inspect nearby chars for context.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray: Deletes the element at index `which` from a cJSON array. Use it on a valid array and zero-based index. It detaches the item, then frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If the index is out of range or array is invalid, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject: Deletes the first object member with the given key. Use it on a cJSON object and key string; it detaches the matching item, then frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If no match exists, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray: Replaces the array element at index `which` with `newitem`. Use on a cJSON array with `which >= 0`; it looks up the item and delegates replacement by pointer. Returns `false` for negative index or if replacement fails.
functions.cJSON_AddBoolToObject: Creates a JSON boolean child and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it with a valid object; it returns the new bool item on success, or `NULL` if creation/addition fails. On failure, the temporary item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_Duplicate: `cJSON_Duplicate` creates a copy of a `cJSON` item. Use it on an existing node; pass `recurse=1` to deep-copy arrays/objects and their children, `0` to copy only the item itself. If `item` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateIntArray: Creates a JSON array from `count` ints. Use with a valid `numbers` pointer and nonnegative `count`; `count` must not exceed the source array length. Returns `NULL` if `count < 0`, `numbers == NULL`, or allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObject: Detaches the first object member matching `string` and returns it. Use on a JSON object to remove an item without deleting it. If `object`/`string` is invalid or no match exists, it returns `NULL` (via `cJSON_GetObjectItem`/detach).
functions.cJSON_IsNumber: `cJSON_IsNumber` checks whether a `cJSON*` points to a non-NULL item whose base type is `cJSON_Number`. Use it to test an item before reading numeric fields. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-number type.
functions.cJSON_Compare: `cJSON_Compare` checks whether two cJSON values are equal. Use it only with valid cJSON nodes; `NULL`, invalid types, or different base types return `false`. Same pointer returns `true`. `case_sensitive` controls object-key comparison.
functions.cJSON_Delete: Deletes a cJSON item and all owned descendants. Call it on a root node when done. It walks `next` siblings, frees `child`, `valuestring`, and `string` unless marked `cJSON_IsReference`/`cJSON_StringIsConst`, then frees each node.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray: Adds a reference copy of `item` to `array` (not the original). Use it to reuse an existing cJSON node without transferring ownership. Returns false if `array` is NULL; otherwise appends a reference created from `item`.
functions.cJSON_GetNumberValue: `cJSON_GetNumberValue` returns a JSON number as `double`. Use it only on numeric items; otherwise it returns `NAN`. It’s a safe accessor that checks `cJSON_IsNumber(item)` before reading `item->valuedouble`.
functions.cJSON_IsString: `cJSON_IsString` is a type-check helper. Use it to test whether a `cJSON*` points to a JSON string node. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-string item; otherwise `true` when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_String`.
functions.cJSON_PrintUnformatted: `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` serializes a `cJSON` item to compact JSON text with no spaces/newlines, suitable for storage or transmission. Use it on a valid `cJSON*`; it returns a newly allocated `char*` you must free with cJSON’s free hook. Returns `NULL` on failure.
functions.cJSON_GetArraySize: `cJSON_GetArraySize` counts linked `child` nodes in a cJSON array/object and returns that count as `int`. Use it on a valid cJSON container; `NULL` returns 0. Empty arrays/objects return 0. It may overflow for very large sizes.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer: Detaches `item` from `parent`’s array/object without deleting it. Use only with a child of `parent`; it returns the detached node or `NULL` if `parent/item` is `NULL` or `item` isn’t linked to `parent`. It fixes sibling links and clears parent links.
functions.cJSON_CreateArray: `cJSON_CreateArray()` creates a new empty `cJSON` array node. Use it when building JSON trees, then add elements with the cJSON add-item APIs. It returns a newly allocated array item, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_SetNumberHelper: Helper for `cJSON_SetNumberValue`: set a `cJSON` number’s `valueint` (clamped to `INT_MIN/INT_MAX`) and `valuedouble`. Use on a valid number item; it returns the stored double.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Deletes an object member by **case-sensitive key**. Use it on a cJSON object plus a key string; it detaches the matching item and then frees it. If no matching item exists, nothing happens.
functions.cJSON_Version: `cJSON_Version()` returns a static, null-terminated string with the library version (`major.minor.patch`). Call it with no args to read the cJSON version. It formats the value each call and returns the same internal buffer.
functions.cJSON_Minify: `cJSON_Minify` edits a writable JSON buffer in place to remove whitespace and comments. Pass a non-NULL, mutable `char*`; it returns void. If `json==NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.cJSON_InsertItemInArray: Inserts `newitem` into `array` at index `which`. Use with a valid array and non-NULL item; negative index fails. If `which` is past the end, it appends. Returns false on invalid/corrupt array state, otherwise links the item into the list.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts: Parses JSON from a buffer with known length. Use when input may not be NUL-terminated; `return_parse_end` gets the stop position. Fails on `NULL`/0 length or parse errors, and can require trailing `\0` if `require_null_terminated` is true.
functions.cJSON_CreateObjectReference: Creates a reference wrapper for an existing object/array node. Use it when you want `cJSON_Delete` to free only the wrapper, not the referenced child tree. On allocation failure it returns `NULL`; otherwise it sets type to `cJSON_Object | cJSON_IsReference` and stores `child`.
functions.cJSON_CreateArrayReference:
Creates a cJSON array node that **references** an existing child list, not a copy. Use it to wrap already-built items as an array. On success it returns the new node; on allocation failure it returns `NULL`. The referenced children aren’t owned/copied.
This crash is due to API misuse. cJSON_CreateArrayReference(NULL) still allocates a cJSON wrapper object and returns it; passing NULL does not make it a no-op. Always capture the returned pointer and call cJSON_Delete() on it when no longer needed. Prefer guarding the call with a NULL check on the child argument, e.g. only call cJSON_CreateArrayReference(child) when child != NULL, or if testing NULL-input behavior, immediately delete the returned object if non-NULL.
functions.cJSON_InitHooks: Sets cJSON’s global allocators. Pass `hooks` to override malloc/free; `realloc` is enabled only when both custom hooks are absent (default malloc/free). Pass `NULL` to reset to standard `malloc/free/realloc`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithOpts: `cJSON_ParseWithOpts` parses a JSON string like `cJSON_Parse`, but lets you: 1) require a NUL-terminated input, and 2) get the parse end/error pointer. Pass `return_parse_end` to know where parsing stopped; on failure it points to the error. Returns `NULL` if `value` is `NULL` or parse fails.
